guide.03: Dewrito runs two chat services. Matrix is the open, federated network where most of our community lives. Fluxer is a self-hosted, Discord-style app. You can use one or both. This guide takes about ten minutes.
guide.04: Before you begin: you need an email address from a provider on our allowed list. There is a checker on the register page. Accounts are for people 18 and over, per the terms.
guide.05: Create your Matrix account Matrix
guide.06: Registration happens through Sable, the web client we host. It is pre-pointed at our homeserver, so you only fill in a username, password and email.
guide.08: Check your inbox for the verification email and click the link. Your full Matrix ID will be @yourname:dewrito.net. That is the address people use to find you anywhere on the Matrix network, not only on our server.
guide.09: Write down your password. Matrix encrypts private rooms on your device. If you lose both your password and your recovery key (step 4), nobody, including us, can recover your encrypted history.
guide.11: Matrix is a protocol, so any Matrix app works with your Dewrito account. When an app asks for your homeserver, enter dewrito.net. The app discovers the rest on its own.
guide.14: The client you registered with. Nothing to install, open it in any browser. Based on Cinny.
guide.18: Clean, Discord-like layout, running on our own server. Sable is built on it, so switching between the two feels natural.
guide.22: Simple and friendly, especially on phones. A good pick if you want something that just works.
guide.26: A comfortable, privacy-respecting client with voice chat, a shared calendar and photo albums, and several accounts signed in at once.
guide.30: A fork of Commet that aims to feel like Discord: familiar layout, themes and voice. Unofficial and still in testing.
guide.32: You can sign in on several devices at once. Each one shows up as a session you can name and sign out from in your account settings.
guide.34: A space is a folder of rooms. Our official space holds the general chat, announcements and the rooms our members run. Join it and everything else is one click away.
guide.36: The link opens a matrix.to page that hands you to whichever client you installed. On Sable, paste #dewrito:dewrito.net into the search box instead.
guide.37: Say hello in #dewrito_general:dewrito.net, the main chat room.
guide.38: Open the space in your client and pick the rooms you want to see. Leaving a room never leaves the space.
guide.39: Looking for communities outside our space? The directory lists rooms across the Matrix network and Fluxer servers, with member counts and descriptions.
guide.41: Do this once, in the first client you set up. It takes a minute and protects your encrypted messages.
guide.42: Set up key backup. In your client's security settings, enable "secure backup" and save the recovery key somewhere safe, such as a password manager.
guide.43: Verify new devices. When you sign in somewhere new, your existing session asks you to verify it with emoji. Do it. Unverified sessions cannot read your encrypted history.
guide.44: Turn on notifications in the mobile app settings if you want pings for mentions and direct messages.
guide.46: Fluxer is a separate account from Matrix. It feels like Discord: servers, channels, roles, voice and video, screen sharing. Nothing federates to other instances, and nothing leaves our hardware.
guide.49: Create your account and join our community with the invite link.
guide.53: Phone and desktop apps come from the Fluxer project. Point them at fluxer.dewrito.net when asked for an instance.
guide.55: Fluxer is a young project, so expect the occasional rough edge. The source is public at github.com/fluxerapp/fluxer.
guide.57: Bridges. A Discord bridge bot runs on our homeserver. If you run a Discord server and want a room bridged, ask in the general room.
guide.58: Reporting. Use your client's report feature, or email abuse@dewrito.net. Our moderation page explains what happens next.
guide.59: Service problems? Check the status page before assuming it is your connection.
guide.60: Stuck? Contact us. Registration and email-whitelist questions are the most common, and we answer them.
mod.02: How we keep the lights on and the trolls out
mod.03: The rules are in the Terms of Service. This page is about enforcement: who does it, how reports are handled, and which servers we keep out of the directory.
mod.05: In short: illegal content, harassment, spam, and anything that puts the server or other users at risk. The full list is in sections 3 to 5 of the terms. We do not act on good-faith disagreement, tone complaints or lawful discussion we happen to dislike.
mod.09: Use your client's report option on the message, or email abuse@dewrito.net. Include the room, the user, roughly when, and a screenshot if you have one.
mod.12: A moderator reviews the report, usually within a day. Reports from other homeserver admins about our users get the same treatment.
mod.15: Depending on severity: a warning, message removal, a room ban, a server-wide ban, or account deactivation. Illegal material is removed immediately and reported where the law requires.
mod.18: Think we got it wrong? Email support@dewrito.net. A different moderator reviews appeals where possible.
mod.19: Reports made through a Matrix client only reach our moderators, even when the reported user is on another server. For users elsewhere, their own homeserver's admins need to hear from you too. Our admin contacts are published in the standard /.well-known/matrix/support file so other servers can reach us the same way.
mod.21: Draupnir, a moderation bot, applies bans and redactions across the rooms in our space and subscribes to shared ban lists for known spam and abuse accounts.
mod.22: Email whitelist at registration, which stops most throwaway-account spam before it starts. Providers can be added on request.
mod.23: Federation controls on the homeserver for servers that are a persistent source of abuse.
mod.24: On Fluxer, server owners manage their own roles and bans; instance moderators step in for terms violations.
mod.26: Anyone can submit a listing to the Boosted Communities page, so it has its own checks:
mod.27: A captcha and a review step before a listing is created.
mod.28: NSFW listings are hidden behind an age confirmation and never appear in the home-page bar.
mod.29: A word filter on names and descriptions, and a flag moderators can set to pull a listing without deleting it.
mod.30: A blocklist of homeservers whose rooms are never listed, shown below. Boost payments for excluded listings are not refunded.
mod.33: Think a server is on this list by mistake? Tell us.
mod.35: We are a small volunteer team. We do not publish per-case details, but we will say when a rule changes, and we post service-affecting moderation actions, such as blocking a server, as notices on the status page.

privacy.03: Last updated: October 31, 2026. This explains what Dewrito.net stores about you, why, and how to get it removed.
privacy.04: Dewrito.net is a community-run Matrix homeserver and Fluxer instance. We are volunteers, not a company, and we keep only what is needed to run the services and keep them safe. Questions go to support@dewrito.net.
privacy.07: Your username, a hashed password, and the email address you registered with. The email is used for verification, password resets and, rarely, to contact you about your account.
privacy.08: Session records: the devices you are signed in on, their IP addresses and user agents, and when they were last seen. You can view and remove sessions in your client's settings.
privacy.10: Matrix: messages, files, reactions, room state and membership for every room you take part in. In encrypted rooms we store the encrypted payload and cannot read it. In unencrypted rooms, and for all metadata (who, when, which room), we can.
privacy.11: Fluxer: messages, uploads, voice and video session metadata, server and role membership. Fluxer does not encrypt messages end to end.
privacy.12: Uploaded media is stored on our servers until you or a room moderator deletes it, or we remove it for a policy reason.
privacy.14: Our web servers and homeserver write access logs containing IP addresses, timestamps and requested URLs. We keep them for a short period for debugging and abuse handling, then delete them.
privacy.16: Matrix is federated. When you join a room that has members on other homeservers, your messages, profile name, avatar and Matrix ID are sent to those servers so their users can see them. Those copies are governed by the other servers' policies, and we cannot delete them. The same applies to direct messages with users elsewhere. Fluxer does not federate; its data stays on our hardware.
privacy.18: Hosting and management: our Matrix homeserver runs on infrastructure managed with etke.cc tooling. Their staff may access server data when we ask for support.
privacy.19: Voice and video calls on Matrix go through a LiveKit service we host at matrix.dewrito.net. Call media is relayed, not recorded.
privacy.20: Identity server: clients are pointed at vector.im for contact discovery. It only receives data if you explicitly choose to share your email or phone number in your client settings.
privacy.21: Community directory: listings you submit on the Boosted Communities page are stored in a Supabase database and are public. Boost payments are recorded on the public Stellar ledger, which is permanent and visible to anyone.
privacy.22: Donations: handled by Ko-fi and NOWPayments under their own policies. We receive the amount and whatever name or message you choose to attach, not your payment details.
privacy.23: This website: loads fonts from Google Fonts, the Ko-fi widget on the home page, and Google reCAPTCHA on the directory page. These providers see your IP address and browser details when those resources load. The site sets no cookies of its own. If we enable usage analytics, we will use a cookie-free, self-hosted tool and name it here.
privacy.25: To run the services you signed up for, to keep them secure, to enforce the Terms of Service, to respond to abuse reports, and to meet legal obligations. We do not sell data, run advertising, or profile users.
privacy.27: Volunteer moderators can read unencrypted rooms they are in, see membership of any room on our server, and view reports you submit. A moderation bot (Draupnir) acts on bans and redactions. Details are on the moderation page.
privacy.29: Deactivating your account (in your client's settings, or by emailing support) removes your profile, ends all sessions and stops the email being used. Messages you sent remain in rooms unless you also ask for them to be erased; most Matrix clients offer this at deactivation.
privacy.30: Erased messages are redacted on our server and a redaction is sent to federated servers, which usually honour it but are not obliged to.
privacy.31: You can request a copy of your data, or deletion, by emailing support@dewrito.net from your registered address. We answer within 30 days.
privacy.33: If you are in the EU, UK or another jurisdiction with data-protection law, you have the right to access, correct, export and erase your data, and to object to processing. The section above is how to exercise them. You can also complain to your local supervisory authority.
privacy.35: Our services are for adults. We do not knowingly keep accounts for anyone under 18 and will remove them when identified.
privacy.37: We will post changes here and update the date at the top. Significant changes are announced on the status page and in the Dewrito space.
bh.02: Get your Matrix room or Fluxer server featured on the Dewrito homepage slider and community directory using decentralized ledger rewards.
bh.03: Our promotional showcase operates completely on chain. By sending a qualifying transaction over the Stellar network, our automated daemon tracks metrics and pushes your listing directly into our high-visibility rotation slider.
bh.05: Every community registered in our database is assigned a unique tracking token identifier key.
bh.06: Navigate to the main Boosted Communities portal page.
bh.07: Fill out the details to Create Your Boost Memo, and double check everything.
bh.08: Copy the exact text string shown under the "Promo/Memo Key" label.
bh.09: Important Configuration Note: You must provide this precise memo or your listing will not show up. If you have issues, contact support.
bh.11: Each individual slot boost transaction tier adds 30 days of active visibility validation status.
bh.12: Base Tier Rate: 25 XLM balances exactly 1 full promotion month cycle.
bh.13: Issue the transaction from your preferred asset wallet to our infrastructure hub node address:
bh.14: Easiest: in the boost window on the directory, pick a duration and tap Open in Stellar wallet or scan the QR code. Wallets such as Lobstr, Solar, Freighter or xBull open with the address, amount and memo already filled in.
bh.15: Otherwise use any wallet or exchange that supports memos, such as Coinbase.
bh.16: Ensure your wallet interface transaction has a Memo Field.
bh.17: Paste your copied Memo into the input field line.
